blocks.text: How to Structure a Night-Shift Custodial Capex & Opex Worksheet

When corporate controllers review an in-house janitorial proposal for after-hours cleaning, the initial estimate frequently omits up to 42% of the true annual operating expenditure. Standard payroll templates built for daytime administrative staff fail to account for three night-shift realities: mandatory hourly wage differentials required to attract evening labor, elevated workers' compensation experience modification rates for solo custodial work, and the hardware capital expenditure required to monitor and equip an unsupervised employee after 6:00 PM.

Furthermore, any valid financial comparison between W-2 direct hires and outsourced building service contractors (BSCs) must normalize monthly labor hours using the commercial real estate accounting standard of 4.333 weeks per month (52 weeks divided by 12 months). Multiplying a 5-night schedule by 4.0 weeks instead of 4.333 weeks understates annual payroll, chemical replenishment, and overtime relief budgets by a full month of operation every year.

blocks.title: Accounting Rule: The 4.333 Weeks-Per-Month Multiplier
blocks.text: A 5-night-per-week cleaning schedule equals 260 annual shifts, or exactly 21.65 visits per month (5 visits x 4.333 weeks). If your night custodian works 4.5 hours per shift, you must budget for 97.43 base payroll hours per month (1,169.1 hours per year)—plus at least 110 hours per year of paid vacation, sick leave, and holiday coverage.

The spreadsheet template below models a representative 15,000-square-foot commercial office with mixed flooring (1.05x multiplier: 11,000 sq ft commercial carpet and 4,000 sq ft VCT/ceramic tile), four multi-stall restrooms ($15 to $30 per-visit benchmark scope), a staff breakroom ($12 to $25 per-visit scope), and glass conference partitions ($15 to $35 per-visit scope). At the ISSA production benchmark of 3,500 square feet per hour adjusted for mixed flooring, the facility requires 4.5 paid hours per night across 21.65 monthly visits.

Under-equipping a solo night worker with light-duty residential tools slows production below 2,500 square feet per hour and increases ergonomic strain injuries.

Lone-Worker Safety & Access Control Hardware ($250 to $480 Upfront Capex): A ruggedized IP67 cellular man-down wearable device with tilt-sensor alarm, a wall-mounted first-aid and OSHA bloodborne pathogen spill kit, and a biometric or PIN-authenticated key cabinet inside the janitor closet.

Closed-Loop Chemical Inventory & Surface Care Stock ($350 to $620 Initial Stocking): Bulk case packs of multi-surface peroxide cleaner, glass cleaner, and VCT floor care chemistry to prevent mid-month emergency retail purchases.

Glass & Partition Detailing Chemistry: Stock the Zep Commercial Streak-Free Glass Cleaner Gallon (4-Case), an ammonia-based rapid-dry refillable formula engineered to remove fingerprints from lobby curtain walls and interior glass conference partitions without leaving hazy residue under morning sunlight.

Periodic Hard-Floor Restoration Chemistry: Budget one semi-annual order of the Zep High-Traffic Floor Polish & Stripper Bundle (2 x 1-gallon acrylic finish and commercial VCT stripper combo) to restore wet-look gloss on vinyl corridors during scheduled two-person weekend maintenance.

blocks.text: Step-by-Step Procurement Audit Checklist Before Approving In-House Night Staff

items.name: Step 1: Verify Workers' Compensation Class Code & Experience Mod Impact
items.text: Request a pro-forma premium calculation from your commercial insurance broker showing the exact cost of adding night custodial payroll under NCCI Code 9015 or 9014, including the impact of a single lost-time night claim on your company-wide Experience Modification Rate (EMR).

items.name: Step 2: Price Mandatory Lone-Worker Safety Infrastructure
items.text: Obtain binding quotes for cellular man-down panic badges, 24/7 monitoring center dispatch, and door-prop alarm sensors. Never approve an unsupervised night-shift budget that omits automated welfare verification.

items.name: Step 3: Audit Nighttime Relief and Supervision Coverage
items.text: Identify by name which salaried manager or cross-trained employee will drive to the office at 8:00 PM when the night custodian calls out sick, and add their loaded overtime rate (plus 12 annual inspection visits) to line 6 of your worksheet.

items.name: Step 4: Benchmark Against 3 Fixed-Fee Outsourced Night Proposals
items.text: Solicit three itemized commercial janitorial bids calculated at 21.65 visits per month (5x/week with the 0.90 frequency multiplier), verifying that each bidder includes a $1M/$2M General Liability policy, statutory Workers' Compensation, and a $50,000+ Employee Dishonesty Bond.

blocks.title: Isolate Paper & Soap Consumables on Line 12
blocks.text: Whether you staff in-house or outsource, always track restroom paper towels, toilet tissue, hand soap, and can liners ($0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit, or $390 to $810/month for a 15,000 sq ft office) on a separate general ledger line. Keeping consumables separate prevents contractors from padding labor bids and allows accurate apples-to-apples labor comparisons.

faqs.q: Why must janitorial budget worksheets use 4.333 weeks per month instead of 4 weeks?
faqs.a: There are 52 weeks in a calendar year, which divided by 12 months equals 4.333 weeks per month. Four months every year contain five full workweeks instead of four. Budgeting a 5x/week night cleaner at 20 shifts per month instead of 21.65 shifts underfunds your annual payroll and supply ledger by 19.8 shifts (nearly 90 labor hours) per year.

faqs.q: What equipment amortization period should controllers use for commercial janitorial hardware?
faqs.a: Commercial backpack vacuums, dual-compartment wringer buckets, utility carts, and microfiber pulse mop frames should be amortized over 36 months (3 years) for daily night-shift use, with an additional 12% to 15% annual maintenance allowance for replacement HEPA filters, vacuum hoses, brush strips, and launderable microfiber pads.

faqs.q: How much shift differential is required to hire a dependable night custodian in 2026?
faqs.a: Across most US metro commercial markets, recruiting a background-checked W-2 custodian for an unsupervised 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM or 10:00 PM to 6:30 AM shift requires a $1.50 to $3.00 per hour shift premium above daytime porter rates (typically adding 8% to 15% to base wages), alongside guaranteed minimum weekly hours.

faqs.q: Which insurance certificates replace in-house liability lines when outsourcing night cleaning?
faqs.a: When you outsource night cleaning, require the vendor to furnish an ACORD 25 Certificate of Insurance naming your company and the property landlord as Additional Insureds on a $1M/$2M Commercial General Liability policy, statutory Workers' Compensation with a Waiver of Subrogation, a $50,000 to $100,000 Third-Party Employee Dishonesty (Janitorial) Bond, and Commercial Auto coverage if mobile route vans enter your garage.
